0.name: TEXT_REGFSTAETHERYTEGUID_00032_NICIA_000_1
0.description: Greetings, adventurer. I have been assigned this post to answer any queries citizens may have regarding aetherial travel. Is there aught you would like to ask?

4.name: TEXT_REGFSTAETHERYTEGUID_00032_A1_000_3
4.description: What is the difference between Return and Teleport?

6.name: TEXT_REGFSTAETHERYTEGUID_00032_NICIA_000_10
6.description: Before one might understand aetherial travel, one must first understand the substance that makes it possible─aether.

7.name: TEXT_REGFSTAETHERYTEGUID_00032_NICIA_000_11
7.description: What is aether, you ask? Why, only the source of all being! Though it cannot be seen, it is everywhere...or should I say, it is every<hex:021A020203>thing<hex:021A020103>.

8.name: TEXT_REGFSTAETHERYTEGUID_00032_NICIA_000_12
8.description: Aether flows around us and within us, and without it we would cease to exist.

9.name: TEXT_REGFSTAETHERYTEGUID_00032_NICIA_000_13
9.description: When we die, it is believed that the shock separates our spirits from our corporeal forms. Our bodies are then broken down and are absorbed back into the aetherial river, while the soul is left to journey to its final destination in the afterlife. Some call this “returning to the Lifestream.”

10.name: TEXT_REGFSTAETHERYTEGUID_00032_NICIA_000_14
10.description: However, our ancestors discovered ways in which, through meditation and focus of spiritual energies, one could reduce her body to aether without losing the grip on her soul, in turn allowing for travel upon the Lifestream. These methods have been given the names Return and Teleport.

11.name: TEXT_REGFSTAETHERYTEGUID_00032_NICIA_000_20
11.description: As you travel through Eorzea, you will oft come across large floating deposits of a crystalline substance known as aetheryte. The one before us here is a fine example.

12.name: TEXT_REGFSTAETHERYTEGUID_00032_NICIA_000_21
12.description: It is said that aetheryte is the solid manifestation of the planet's lifeblood, aether, and that by touching it, the aether which makes up our bodies resonates with that contained in the crystal. This is called “attunement.”

13.name: TEXT_REGFSTAETHERYTEGUID_00032_NICIA_000_22
13.description: Normally, when one's body is reduced to aether, it will naturally gravitate to the location with which it resonates the greatest─or one's “home point.” This is why upon losing consciousness in battle, many wake to find themselves back at an aetheryte.

14.name: TEXT_REGFSTAETHERYTEGUID_00032_NICIA_000_23
14.description: In other words, aetherytes act as lodestones, assuring that the body, in its aetherial form, is not lost to the pull of the greater flow.

15.name: TEXT_REGFSTAETHERYTEGUID_00032_NICIA_000_24
15.description: And, because signatures of past attunements are maintained within our bodies, it is possible (with some spiritual training, of course) to ignore the pull back to the strongest resonation, and travel to another beacon. Many refer to this as “Teleportation.”

16.name: TEXT_REGFSTAETHERYTEGUID_00032_NICIA_000_25
16.description: What is even more amazing is that when teleporting, we can “carry” those with whom we have created a bond, such as an adventuring party─assuming they have previously attuned with the destination aetheryte.

17.name: TEXT_REGFSTAETHERYTEGUID_00032_NICIA_000_30
17.description: As Return merely involves allowing the body to be drawn back to the strongest aetherial beacon─one's home point─it is fairly easy to execute and requires very little spiritual exertion.

18.name: TEXT_REGFSTAETHERYTEGUID_00032_NICIA_000_31
18.description: Usually, a few moments of rest is all that is needed before it is safe to attempt another jump.

19.name: TEXT_REGFSTAETHERYTEGUID_00032_NICIA_000_32
19.description: Teleportation, on the other hand, comes with a greater price. A great deal of spiritual energy known as “anima” is required to fight the natural flow of the Lifestream and guide one's body and soul to a comparatively weak aetherial beacon.

20.name: TEXT_REGFSTAETHERYTEGUID_00032_NICIA_000_33
20.description: If one's body lacks sufficient anima, teleporting to a location may prove impossible. Luckily for most of us, anima is restored quickly and should not prohibit regular travel.

21.name: TEXT_REGFSTAETHERYTEGUID_00032_NICIA_000_34
21.description: Then why, you ask, must we pay gil when using Teleport? Well, after the Calamity, many of the existing aetheryte camps were destroyed. To relocate and rebuild them required a large sum of money, much of which was lent by certain men of business from Ul'dah.

22.name: TEXT_REGFSTAETHERYTEGUID_00032_NICIA_000_35
22.description: The gil you pay when either leaving from or arriving at an aetheryte goes to paying off that debt.
